hub.meta_title: Letting agents in London | Hello New Home
hub.meta_description: London letting agents: management capped at £150 a month, no VAT, no lock-in. South East London first, with a Local Partner and head office compliance.
hub.intro: Hello New Home opens in London one zone at a time, with a Local Partner who lives in it and a head office that does the regulated work. Our first zone is South East London: SE1 to SE28, Bromley's BR1 to BR7 and the Bexley DA districts, covering Southwark, east Lambeth, Lewisham, Greenwich, Bromley and Bexley. Full management is 12% of rent, capped at £150 a month, no VAT, no lock-in. On London rents the cap matters more than anywhere else we work.

sections.h2: Where we start, and how it works
sections.html:
We begin with South East London because it is one rail corridor out of London Bridge with the widest spread of rents in the capital, from Southwark flats at £2,474 a month to outer Bexley houses well below that. Leads are routed by postcode district: if your property is elsewhere in London we say honestly whether we can look after it yet, and more zones open as partners join.

Our Local Partner does the viewings, quarterly inspections, move-ins and the handover from your current agent. Head office does the agreement and written statement of terms, Right to Rent checks, deposit protection, rent collection, the repairs desk, the borough licence and the compliance calendar. We belong to a redress scheme and a client money protection scheme, both named on our fee sheet; the Local Partner never holds your money.

sections.h2: Why London landlords switch: the cap
sections.html:
The ONS average private rent for London was £2,332 a month in August 2026, up 3.5% on the year from £2,253, against £1,459 across England. At 12% a London agent takes £280 a month from that rent; many charge 12% plus VAT, which is £336, with a 12-month tie-in.

We charge £150, because that is where the cap is, with nothing added for VAT. On the London average that is £130 a month and £1,560 a year you keep. On a Southwark flat at the borough average of £2,474 a 12% fee would be £297; ours is still £150. You can leave with 30 days' notice, and the fee sheet has no renewal, inspection or notice charges.

sections.h2: Borough licensing in South East London
sections.html:
London licensing is decided borough by borough, and since December 2024 a council can start a selective scheme of any size without government approval. We check the current designation for every address before marketing and write it into your management agreement.

  • Southwark: borough-wide additional licensing to 28 February 2027, plus selective licensing in two designations running to 28 February 2027 and 31 October 2028, the latter including Peckham, Camberwell Green and Rotherhithe.
  • Lewisham: selective licensing across 18 wards to 30 June 2029, around 20,000 homes, plus borough-wide additional licensing to 4 April 2027.
  • Greenwich: borough-wide additional HMO licensing and selective licensing in some wards; a consultation on extending it to 18 wards closed on 12 October 2026 and a decision is awaited.
  • Bexley: selective licensing in Belvedere ward from 13 January 2025 to 12 January 2030.
  • Bromley: mandatory HMO licensing only at the last published assessment.

Letting without a required licence risks a civil penalty of up to £30,000 and a rent repayment order. The application is part of management.

sections.h2: The streets and who rents them
sections.html:
• Bermondsey and Rotherhithe (SE1, SE16): professionals near London Bridge, Guy's and St Thomas', at the top of the zone's rent range.
  • Peckham and Camberwell (SE15, SE5): flats and shared houses for King's College Hospital staff and young professionals, inside Southwark's selective licensing.
  • Lewisham and Catford (SE13, SE6): family houses and flats near University Hospital Lewisham, in the borough's selective licensing area.
  • Greenwich and Woolwich (SE10, SE18): Elizabeth line service from Woolwich since 24 May 2022 has widened the tenant pool to Canary Wharf and central London.
  • Bromley (BR1 to BR7): family long lets in a borough with mandatory HMO licensing only, at rents that still clear the £150 cap.
  • Bexleyheath and Belvedere (DA6, DA7, DA17): the outer edge of the zone, with rents well below Southwark's and a selective licence needed in Belvedere.

sections.h2: Long let, short let and the 90-night rule
sections.html: London is the one place where a whole-home short let has a hard limit: 90 nights in a calendar year without planning permission, and every stay of fewer than 90 consecutive nights counts. We run both, so our London appraisal has three columns: the property as a tenancy; as 90 nights of short stays then a let of 90 nights or more; and as 90 nights of short stays then a tenancy. Flex Switch moves it between them with no re-onboarding. The short-let page has the detail.

Start with a free rent review. Give us the address and we call within one working day with a realistic rent for your street, the borough licensing position, and a written comparison of £150 against the fee you pay now. If short stays might pay, ask for the free short-let appraisal instead and you get all three columns. Our Local Partner will come to the property anywhere in the zone.

faqs.q: Which parts of London do you cover?
faqs.a: Our first zone is South East London: SE1 to SE28, BR1 to BR7 and the Bexley DA districts, covering Southwark, east Lambeth, Lewisham, Greenwich, Bromley and Bexley. Further zones open as Local Partners join. Send the postcode and we tell you straight away whether we can take it on.

faqs.q: How much does full management cost in London?
faqs.a: 12% of rent, capped at £150 a month, with no VAT added. On the London average rent of £2,332 a 12% fee would be £280; ours is £150. There are no renewal, inspection or notice fees, and you can leave with 30 days' notice.

faqs.q: Does my London property need a licence?
faqs.a: It depends on the borough and often the ward. Southwark, Lewisham and Greenwich run additional and selective schemes, Bexley licenses Belvedere ward, and Bromley has mandatory HMO licensing only. We check the current designation for every address before marketing and complete the application.

Our Local Partner in South East London does viewings, inspections and move-ins. Head office handles the agreement, Right to Rent checks, deposit, rent collection, repairs desk and licensing. The agreement is with Hello New Home and the Local Partner never holds your money.

faqs.q: Can I short let my London flat?
faqs.a: For up to 90 nights a calendar year without planning permission, and every stay under 90 consecutive nights counts. After that the lawful options are a let of 90 nights or more or a tenancy. We run both and the free appraisal shows all three columns.

lettings.meta_title: Property management in London | Hello New Home
lettings.meta_description: Full property management in South East London: 12% of rent, capped at £150 a month, no VAT. Borough licence, Right to Rent and Renters' Rights Act handled.
lettings.intro: In London the question is not whether an agent will manage your flat but what it costs and what you are tied into. Ours is 12% of rent, capped at £150 a month, no VAT, no 12-month agreement, 30 days' notice to leave. Our Local Partner in South East London does the visits; head office does the agreement, the borough licence, Right to Rent, the deposit and the rent. You get a statement every month and a call when something matters.

sections.html:
• Photographs, floorplan, EPC and the licence number on the listing where a scheme applies, on Rightmove, Zoopla and OnTheMarket, with viewings by our Local Partner.
  • Referencing through Vouch or Goodlord, a Right to Rent check on each adult occupier, and the agreement and written statement of terms served before the tenancy is agreed.
  • A clear asking rent, no bidding above it, and no more than one month's rent in advance, as the Renters' Rights Act requires.
  • Deposit protected within 30 days and capped at five weeks' rent; holding deposit held to one week.
  • Rent collection, arrears chasing and a repairs desk answered 24 hours a day.
  • Quarterly inspections by someone who lives in the zone, with a written report.
  • The borough licence application where your address needs one, and every certificate and expiry on the compliance calendar.
  • An annual rent review and a year-end statement.

The Southwark averages from the ONS for August 2026 show how the cap works in the zone. A one-bed at £1,876 would cost £225 a month at 12%; we charge £150. A two-bed at £2,348 would cost £282; we charge £150. A three-bed at £2,732 would cost £328; we charge £150. On the three-bed that is £178 a month and £2,136 a year kept, and more again against an agent adding VAT.

The cap starts at £1,250 a month, so in South East London it applies to almost every property we take on. Tenant Find alone is £495, no let no fee, and includes marketing, viewings, referencing, Right to Rent, the agreement, the written statement, deposit registration and the inventory.

sections.h2: The Renters' Rights Act in a London letting
sections.html:
Since 1 May 2026 every tenancy is periodic and section 21 has gone. The parts London landlords ask about most are the ones aimed at a competitive market: a stated asking rent with no offers above it, no more than one month's rent in advance, and a reply within 28 days to any pet request, refused only on reasonable grounds. Councils have reported penalties of up to £7,000, rising to £40,000 for serious or repeat cases.

Rent rises go by Section 13 notice, once in 12 months, with two months' notice; a tenant can challenge at the tribunal, which can lower the rent but not raise it. A written statement of terms is required before the tenancy starts. From December 2026 the private rented sector database opens and we complete your registration when London's window arrives. If you need the flat back to live in or to sell, Grounds 1 and 1A need four months' notice and cannot be used in the first 12 months.

Many London agents charge 12% plus VAT with a 12-month tie-in. When yours ends, or sooner if the agreement allows, we take the property over without the tenant moving: notice to the agent, transfer of the deposit and file, a check of the certificates and written statement against the Act and the borough's licensing map, and a visit from our Local Partner so the tenant meets a face. Anything missing is reported before we start.

sections.h2: Next step: the free rent review
sections.html: Send the address through the free rent review. Within one working day you have a realistic rent for your street, the borough licence position for the flat, and a written comparison of £150 a month against your current fee, with and without the VAT your agent may be adding. Nothing is listed until the licence position is on file.

faqs.q: Is the £150 cap really the whole management fee?
faqs.a: Yes. Full management is 12% of rent until that reaches £150, and never more, with no VAT added. There are no renewal, inspection or notice fees. Borough licence fees are council charges and are separate.

faqs.q: Can you take over a flat that is still under a 12-month agreement?
faqs.a: When the agreement allows notice, yes. We serve it, transfer the deposit and file, check the paperwork against the Renters' Rights Act and the borough licensing map, and our Local Partner meets the tenant. Tell us your end date and we work to it.

faqs.q: What is a bidding war ban?
faqs.a: Since 1 May 2026 landlords and agents in England must state a clear asking rent and cannot invite or accept offers above it. We market at the honest figure for the street and hold to it. Councils can fine breaches up to £7,000, rising to £40,000 for repeat cases.

faqs.q: Who applies for the borough licence?
faqs.a: We do, as part of management. Head office checks the current designation for the address, prepares the application with the certificates the borough asks for and tracks the expiry. The borough's fee is paid to the borough.

faqs.q: How often will someone visit the property?
faqs.a: Our Local Partner inspects quarterly and sends a written report with photographs. They also do the move-in, the move-out and any visit a repair needs. Head office runs the repairs desk 24 hours a day.

shortlets.meta_title: Airbnb & short-let management London | Hello New Home
shortlets.meta_description: London short-let management built around the 90-night rule: 90 nights of short stays, then a 90-night-plus let or a tenancy. 18% of net revenue, no VAT.
shortlets.h1: Airbnb and short-let management in London
shortlets.intro: In Greater London a whole home can be short let for no more than 90 nights in a calendar year without planning permission, and every stay of fewer than 90 consecutive nights counts towards that total. Our London offer is built around the rule: 90 nights of short stays, then a let of 90 nights or more or a tenancy, with one agent, one statement and Flex Switch between them. Full SA Management is 18% of net booking revenue.

sections.html:
Under section 25 of the Greater London Council (General Powers) Act 1973, using a London home as temporary sleeping accommodation, meaning a stay by the same person of fewer than 90 consecutive nights, is a change of use needing planning permission. The Deregulation Act 2015 allows up to 90 such nights in a calendar year without permission, provided the person providing the accommodation is liable for council tax.

The cap attaches to the property, counts bookings across every platform, and resets on 1 January. A 30-night corporate stay is still under 90 consecutive nights, so it uses the allowance rather than escaping it. Hosted stays where you live in the home are outside the rule. Westminster opened 499 investigations in 2025. Airbnb's counter blocks entire-home listings at 90 nights, but only on Airbnb, so we run our own.

sections.h2: How we run a London short let within the rule
sections.html:
For the 90 nights we take bookings of any length under 90 consecutive nights and price them for the season, favouring longer stays where they pay: three 30-night bookings use the same allowance as twenty weekends with fewer changeovers. Our counter alerts you at 70 nights and blocks the calendar at 90 on every channel we control.

For the rest of the year the property becomes a let of 90 nights or more, furnished and bills-inclusive for corporate, relocation, insurance and hospital tenants near Guy's and St Thomas', King's and Lewisham, or a tenancy. A 90-night-plus let to an individual as their home will usually be an assured periodic tenancy under the Renters' Rights Act, and we say so before you sign.

• SA Co-Host, 12% of net booking revenue: pricing, guest messages and the listing for the 90 nights; you run the cleaning; we run the night counter. The usual London starting point.
  • Full SA Management, 18% of net booking revenue, cleaning at cost: everything, for the 90 nights and the 90-night-plus lets: guest vetting and messaging around the clock, cleaning and linen, restocking, repairs, reviews and one monthly owner statement.
  • SA Launch, £495: photography, listings, pricing rules, house manual, the borough licensing check, the night counter and the planning position for your address in writing. Waived with 12 months of Full SA Management.

No VAT, no 12-month minimum, and you can leave on 30 days' notice. We do not promise or apply for planning permission beyond 90 nights.

sections.h2: Council tax, the register and the honest answer
sections.html:
A London short let let for fewer than 70 nights a year, or available for fewer than 140, pays council tax rather than business rates, and several boroughs charge a 100% premium on second homes; we check yours. The government has said a national short-let register for England will be running by March 2027; we register your property when it opens.

For many London flats the honest answer is the tenancy column. A Southwark two-bed averages £2,348 a month as a long let, and 90 nights of short stays plus a 275-night tenancy has to beat that after cleaning, platform fees and empty nights. We recommend whichever column is highest.

sections.h2: Next step: the free short-let appraisal
sections.html: Request the free short-let appraisal with the address. You get three figures, as a tenancy, as 90 nights of short stays plus a 90-night-plus let, and as 90 nights of short stays plus a tenancy, each net of every cost, with the borough licensing and planning position in writing. If the tenancy wins, the free rent review figure is the same one and we manage it at £150 a month.

faqs.q: How many nights can I short let my London flat?
faqs.a: Up to 90 nights in a calendar year without planning permission. Every stay of fewer than 90 consecutive nights counts, across all platforms combined, and the count resets on 1 January. Beyond 90 nights you need planning permission, which few boroughs grant for flats.

faqs.q: Does a 30-night corporate let avoid the 90-night rule?
faqs.a: No. A 30-night stay is still a stay of fewer than 90 consecutive nights, so it counts towards the 90. The lawful options after the 90 nights are a let of 90 consecutive nights or more, or a tenancy. We manage both.

faqs.q: What happens when I reach 90 nights?
faqs.a: Our counter alerts you at 70 nights and blocks the calendar at 90 on every channel we control. The property then moves to a let of 90 nights or more, furnished and bills-inclusive, or to a tenancy, under the same agent and the same statement.

faqs.q: How much does London short-let management cost?
faqs.a: SA Co-Host is 12% of net booking revenue. Full SA Management is 18%, cleaning at cost, and covers the 90-night-plus lets as well as the short stays. SA Launch is £495, waived with 12 months of Full SA Management. No VAT is added.

faqs.q: Is a short let worth it in London at all?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Ninety nights of short stays plus a 90-night-plus let can beat a tenancy for a well-placed flat; for many homes the tenancy wins once cleaning, platform fees and empty nights are counted. The free appraisal shows all three columns.
